sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 7.7% a year from $15.4 billion in FY2018 to $25.8 billion in FY2025 [F1][F8][F145], while operating income grew faster at 9.9% [F146] and net income barely moved at 0.4% [F147].
The window is not a smooth compounder: operating margin swung from 30.6% in FY2019 to 15.5% in FY2021, then to 41.3% in FY2023 and 32.1% in FY2025 [F18][F20][F22][F24].

The FY2021 collapse came with a $1.5 billion Mountain Valley Pipeline impairment and unfavorable non-qualifying hedge activity [P63][P68], and the FY2023 rebound followed the absence of such charges and $1,729 million of non-qualifying hedge gains in NEER's net income [P30].
FY2024 revenue fell 5.2% [D201] on lower storm and fuel cost recovery revenues at FPL [P35], and FY2025 recovered 9.8% [D236] on higher storm cost recovery and retail base revenues [P21].
FPL is the revenue base, at 70.5% of FY2025 revenue [D271], and it contributed 5.5pp of the 9.8% FY2025 growth [D273][D236].
FPL's FY2025 revenue increase came from higher storm cost recovery, retail base and storm protection plan cost recovery revenues, partly offset by lower fuel cost recovery [P21].
Profit grew slower than revenue in FY2025: operating income rose 10.7% [D237] against 9.8% revenue growth [D236], an incremental operating margin of 34.8% [D256].

NEER's FY2025 results rose on higher earnings from new investments, with 1,604 MW of wind, 2,859 MW of solar and 1,799 MW of battery storage added [P26], partly offset by higher financing costs [P26].
Per-share performance diverged from net income because the diluted share count rose 305.5% in FY2020 [D76]: EPS diluted fell 0.7% a year over the window [F149] against 0.4% net income growth [F147].
FY2025 operating margin of 32.1% [F24] sits 1.8pp above the 30.3% window median [D300] but well below the 41.3% FY2023 high [D299] and far above the 15.5% FY2021 low [D298].
The FY2025 margin was essentially flat, up 0.3pp [D247], as operating costs grew 10.0% [D249] slightly faster than revenue's 9.8% [D236].
D&A rose to 25.5% of revenue in FY2025 [D224] as depreciation and amortization expense increased $951 million, mainly higher amortization of deferred storm costs of about $1,090 million [P16].

Below the line, the effective tax rate fell to -17.7% in FY2025 [D226], driven by clean energy tax credits that rose about $585 million at NEER [P11], leaving net margin 5.6pp below operating margin [D327].
Other income expense of -$3,750 million in FY2025 [X64] reflects unfavorable non-qualifying hedge activity and higher average debt balances at Corporate and Other [P8].
Operating cash flow of $12.5 billion in FY2025 [F64] was 1.83x net income [D227], below the 1.95x window median [D319] but in line with the utility's typical conversion.
Operating cash flow fell 5.8% in FY2025 [D241] while investing outflow reached $23.9 billion [F72], so free cash flow was deeply negative and funded by $23.4 billion of debt issued [X90].
The swing from net over-recovery to net under-recovery of cost recovery clauses cut FPL's operating cash flow by about $89 million in FY2025, mainly on higher fuel prices [P19].
Capital intensity is high: D&A was 25.5% of revenue [D224] and stock-based compensation only 1.5% of operating cash flow [D228], so conversion is driven by working capital and capex, not equity pay.

Net debt widened for a seventh straight year to $92.2 billion in FY2025 [D231][R2], equal to 357.4% of revenue [D232], the weakest net-cash position of the three utilities peers (0th percentile) [D328], against a peer median net-cash position of -235.4% of revenue [D329].

Long-term debt rose 23.7% to $89.6 billion [F136][D245] while equity grew 9.0% to $54.6 billion [F144][D244], and the current ratio of 0.60x [F128] is still below 1.0x despite being the window high [D305].
Free cash flow was negative, so capital return was debt-funded: dividends of $4.68 billion [X82] were paid with no buybacks [D233], and the diluted share count still rose 0.6% [D251].
Returns remain strong against peers: return on average equity of 13.1% [D235] ranks at the 100th percentile versus an 11.6% peer median [D316][D317].

Net debt has risen every year of the window, from $34.3 billion in FY2018 to $92.2 billion in FY2025 [D9][D231], a 7-year streak [R2] that leaves the balance sheet the most levered in its peer set [D328].
The current ratio of 0.60x in FY2025 [F128] is below 1.0x [R1], though it is the highest level in the window [D305] and typical for a utility funding long-lived plant with short-term debt.
FY2024 revenue fell 5.2% [D201][R3] on lower storm and fuel cost recovery revenues at FPL [P35], a pass-through effect rather than a demand loss.
The FY2025 effective tax rate of -17.7% [D226][R4] reflects clean energy tax credits [P11], which flatter net income and make the 26.5% net margin [F40] hard to compare year to year.

Data quality: FY2019 operating expenses were later reported as $14,257 million against $13,851 million first reported, and the pack uses the first-reported value [X18][R5], so FY2019 margin comparisons carry that caveat.
Operating margin: a FY2026 print below the 30.3% window median [D300] would confirm the post-FY2023 fade, while a return above the 32.1% FY2025 level [F24] would reverse it; watch the FY2026 10-K.
Net debt: another year of increase above the $92.2 billion FY2025 level [D231] would extend the seven-year streak [R2]; a first decline would break it, per the FY2026 cash flow statement.
Operating cash flow conversion: a ratio below the 1.83x FY2025 level [D227] or the 1.95x median [D319] would signal working-capital strain from cost recovery clauses [P19] in the FY2026 10-K.
